text:
claire: Quick sync — editor UI rollout is at 10% canary and we hit a spike in CPU on the serving pool last night. I want to tighten the emergency-disable path before we widen the audience.

claire: Proposal: add a short-circuit toggle that only oncall/SRE + platform lead can flip (2 approvals unless SEV). Log every flip to the central audit service and emit an immediate telemetry ping + slack webhook. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

tariq: +1 on the 2-approver for non-SEV. How do you see the approvals happening practically? GH review? Slack ack?

claire: Not GH — too slow. Idea: a designated vault keyholders group (oncall + platform lead) can approve via the control plane UI or a signed CLI command. If it's flipped via CLI, require both signatures unless the SEV flag is set.

jen: For emergency-only path, we should allow single flip by oncall if SEV severity is declared by pagerduty tag. Otherwise gate. Also need TTL on the disable so it auto-resets unless extended by the same approval flow.

maria: Agree re TTL. Also must add an automatic post-ops checklist: (1) record reason, (2) mark impact (latency/errors), (3) start a short bridge. We can have the UI pre-populate these fields when flipping.

claire: Good. Draft of the minimal CLI usage:

```
# sign+apply a feature toggle change, requires 2 signatures by default
redwoodctl toggle set editor_ui --state off --reason "high CPU on serving pool" --sign @tariq --sign @maria

# emergency override (single signer allowed only if --sev declared)
redwoodctl toggle set editor_ui --state off --reason "sev2: cascade" --sign @tariq --sev
```

claire: The control plane will return a flip id that ops-bot will post to the channel and to the audit API. Example response: `{\"flip_id\":\"flip_20260318_0001\",\"status\":\"applied\"}`

ops-bot: flag editor_ui disabled by tariq (oncall) — flip_id flip_20260318_0001 — reason: "high CPU on serving pool" — audit: https://audit.redwood.internal/flips/flip_20260318_0001 :rotating_light:

tariq: Testing the happy path in staging now. One question: who can extend TTL? only approvers or any platform eng? we should lock that to approvers.

jen: Only approvers. Extensions should create a new flip record (so we have a trail). Also add a machine-readable tag for downstream ingestion: `source=toggle`, `stage=canary`, `initiator=tariq`.

maria: On telemetry side, I'll add a rule to alert if we see >5% error rate within 5m after a flip, and post the chart to the flip record.

claire: Ops checklist for the flip record: who flipped, approvers, TTL, reason, related PR/rollout, impacted routes, rollback steps, monitoring links. We'll enforce presence of all fields in the UI/CLI.

tariq: One more: audit retention — legal wants flips retained 7 years for certain customers. ops-bot should tag flips with customer_impact when the toggle touches dedicated or private deployments.

claire: Good catch. We'll add `customer_impact` optional field and require it for Dedicated/Private rolls. ops-bot should also ping the security channel if that flag is set.

ops-bot: noted — will implement `customer_impact` tagging and cross-post to #eng-security when present.

jen: Can we add a quick check command for SRE to confirm current state + last flips? e.g. `redwoodctl toggle status editor_ui --recent` prints last 5 flips with ids and initiators.

claire: Yes. UX must show current state, last flips, TTL expiration, and a one-click re-enable that goes through the same approval flow.

maria: I'll draft the telemetry dashboard panels and add a link template. Will post the panel IDs here when ready.

tariq: I'll run a dry-run tomorrow during the 11:00 maintenance window and simulate a flip (non-SEV) to validate 2-signer flow.

claire: Thanks — action items:
- tariq: dry-run + results in this thread (due tomorrow)
- jen: add TTL enforcement + extension rules in the toggle service
- maria: telemetry panels and alert rules
- ops-bot: implement audit link + customer_impact tag + cross-post
- claire: update runbook doc with new flow and examples

claire: If we agree, I'll open the PR that wires CLI->control-plane->audit and includes the sample UX text. Approvers please ack by EOD. :v:

jen: Ack

maria: Ack

tariq: Ack, will post dry-run results here after test.
